idea: China clean-energy supply chain research for Western investors
buyer: Energy transition funds and industrial PMs
pain: Western investors cannot see inside Chinese solar, battery and EV supply chains
v1: One supply chain map with pricing and capacity
channel: Her fund network plus father's China energy contacts
verdict: Both networks load-bearing at once, with the strongest tailwind available. Best of the energy cluster.

why.distribution: Fund side is her own warm network; the China side is her father's, giving credibility rather than volume.
why.demand: Transition funds buy supply chain research; nothing tested at this price yet.
why.fmf: Requires institutional analysis plus genuine China energy access - a combination almost nobody in London has.
why.defensibility: The access is the moat and it is close to unreplicable for a Western competitor.
why.leverage: One research product serves every subscriber.
why.time_to_revenue: Building the China-side sourcing first: 3-6 months.
why.tailwind: Energy transition capital plus supply chain anxiety - both structural and both budgeted.
why.ceiling: £2,000/mo x 9 funds = £216k, and transition funds pay these prices.

ceiling_arithmetic: £2,000/mo x 9 funds = £216k gross, less ~£20k translation, data and travel = £196k net on annual contracts. Nine institutional subscribers is a reachable number given her fund network. Realistic year one: 4-5 = £96-120k.
carries: The single most defensible idea in the set: access that a Western competitor genuinely cannot buy, attached to the strongest tailwind and an institutional price point.
kills: Nothing structural. Execution risk is real - geopolitical friction, data compliance, and dependence on her father's goodwill.
test: Ask three transition funds what they cannot see in Chinese supply chains, and ask her father whether two contacts would speak on the record.
test_pass: A fund names a specific blind spot and a contact agrees to talk.
test_fail: Funds say Wood Mackenzie or BNEF covers it adequately.
